newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr pullback no hint of near-term top.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr pullback no hint of near-term top.

text.p: Analysts dismissed the possibility that a dollar pullback after a short-lived foray higher on Wednesday may indicate a topping formation.
The dollar launched an early attack on several big levels, establishing a fresh 47-month high versus the Swiss franc at 1.5261, just above the prior high of 1.5250 set on Monday.
Dollar/yen stopped at 118.95, just short of key 119.00 resistance, or the 50-percent retracement from 126.47, the 1997 high made in May, to 110.62, the year's low set in June.
Dollar/mark ran up to 1.8454 but never challenged its 1.8490 high, the peak since November 1989, made on Monday.
While the pullback from the top was pronounced, the dollar never threatened to breach key supports and bounced back up.
The session's low at 1.8324 marks was well above the key 1.8250 level, or the 38-percent retracement of the move from the July 17 low of 1.7860 to 1.8490, the high on Monday.
The retreat to a 118.13 low never threatened 117.90, the 50-percent retracement of the 116.85/118.95 move this week.

"A very short-term top, yes. But evidence of a significant top is very thin right now," said vice president Rob Kepler at Lehman Brothers who called the dollar's setback "mostly a momentum-based correction as opposed to a critical top."

"Dollar/yen had a 50-percent retreat (of the recent move). Dollar/mark got a small reversal going," said Kepler, who added it would take the loss of 1.8265/75, Tuesday's low, for the dollar's setback to become "a fairly negative event that would dictate a fairly large decline in the dollar."
Analyst Ben Morden at I.D.E.A. agreed "it's a pullback but it would be tough to call a top in dollar/mark or dollar/Swiss before a dip below 1.8172, the recent low or 1.5045/1.50.
"Dollar/mark started to build a weak topping pattern. But dollar/yen has some forward momentum for a break of 119.00 and more importantly, 121.00," Morden stressed.
The 62-percent retracement of the yen's 1997 move is 121.

"A stronger dollar/yen would imply a stronger dollar/mark. There is value around 1.8300/30, nothing truly bearish unless 1.8250 goes," said Morden who added "a mark/Swiss break of 0.8200/20 would signal a more alarming dollar/Swiss selloff."
Dollar/yen was helped by mark/yen's breach of 64.50, a key point in a seven-day bull channel that broke a two-month bear trend. But it was too brief to allow for an attack on 66.00.
Sterling confirmed its correction bottomed out at 2.9725 and at $1.6205.
